messages.author: df74d6fccec2ff7e
messages.subject: unmarkedFrames
parts:
Hi,

I thought I would provide a brief discussion of unmarkedFrames since
they have been the subject of several questions. Many users of R will
be accustomed to using data.frames to supply data to fitting functions
like glm. We decided against this approach for several reasons. First,
wildlife survey data are often associated with metadata that should be
linked to the data, not supplied as arguments to the fitting
functions. Second, we wanted to write custom methods (eg, show,
summary, plot, hist, etc...) for each unmarkedFrame type. Third, R
provides an object-oriented programming style know as S4 that makes it
easy to do the first two things. However, manipulating S4 objects may
not be straight-forward to some, so here is an example that should
provide some guidance. I will eventually clarify these things in the
documentation. For now, see help("unmarkedFrame-class")


# Import
wt <- read.csv(system.file("csv", "widewt.csv", package = "unmarked"))

# Set-up
y <- wt[, 2:4]
siteCovs <- wt[, c("elev", "forest", "length")]
obsCovs <- list(date = wt[, c("date.1", "date.2", "date.3")], ivel =
wt[, c("ivel.1", "ivel.2", "ivel.3")])
wtUMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(y = y, siteCovs = siteCovs, obsCovs = obsCovs)

# Summarize
head(wtUMF)
summary(wtUMF)

# Request the data dimensions
numY(wtUMF)
numSites(wtUMF)
obsNum(wtUMF)

# Extract the y matrix
y <- getY(wtUMF)

# Extract the site covariates as a data.frame
sc <- siteCovs(wtUMF)

# standardize elevation (this could also be done in the formula)
sc$elev <- scale(sc$elev)
siteCovs(wtUMF) <- sc

# Extract the observation covariates as a data.frame in the long format
ocl <- obsCovs(wtUMF)

# Standardize date (this could be done in the formula)
ocl$date <- scale(ocl$date)
obsCovs(wtUMF) <- ocl

# Extract the observation covariates as a list of matrices
oc <- obsCovs(wtUMF, matrices=TRUE)

# Select data from the first 5 sites of the unmarkedFrame
subUMF <- wtUMF[1:5,]

# Select the first survey period
wtUMF1 <- wtUMF[,1]


These are the preferred ways of manipulating unmarkedFrames. If you
want to look at the underlying structure of the data use str:

str(wtUMF)

Note that each component of the object is in a "slot" and slots can be
extracted using the "@" operator.

slotNames(wtUMF)
wtUMF@y # It's better to use getY(wtUMF)


I hope this helps,
Richard
